report.summary: Reviewed chunk 2 of 4 of publish.py: helper functions and render_markdown. Docstring claims largely kept; several uncheckable; one broken (quorum fallback).
risks: publish.py:281-406 | medium | _quorum_counts may report answered=requested when counts are absent, masking a degraded quorum | Check whether any caller passes a verdict with neither list nor ints

publish.py:281-406 | medium | render_markdown docstring promises 'Pure: no I/O' but calls _verbatim, _short, _text, etc. whose I/O behavior is out of this chunk | Inspect those helpers in the rest of the file

publish.py:281-406 | medium | _evidence_paths docstring says 'for the path-marker half of the floor' but no path-marker logic is visible here | Inspect screen_egress and the floor rule in other chunks
publish.py:281-406 | low | render_markdown claims 'EVERY dissent verbatim' but only renders text fields; a dissent with empty text is skipped | Check whether empty dissent text is possible

handoff.purpose: Continue reading publish.py: helper functions (_bus_path, _turns_of, _chain_head, _quorum_counts, _evidence_paths) and the render_markdown function.

symbols.name: _bus_path
symbols.note: Resolves the bus path from transcript or verdict fields, else derives from council_id.

symbols.name: _turns_of
symbols.note: Extracts turn list from transcript: mapping, list/tuple, or object with turns/records/entries field.

symbols.name: _chain_head
symbols.note: Gets chain head digest from transcript/verdict fields, else from last turn's entry_sha.

symbols.name: _quorum_counts
symbols.note: Returns (answered, requested, answered_vendors, missing_vendors) derived from vendor lists or integer fields.

symbols.name: _evidence_paths
symbols.note: Collects evidence paths from verdict evidence/paths fields.

symbols.name: render_markdown
symbols.note: Renders a council deliberation as markdown: outcome, advisory banner, quorum, dissents, convergence, evidence, cost/latency, turns, provenance footer.

claims.text: Explicit field wins; otherwise derived from the council id, which is how bus.py names the file.
claims.why: The code checks transcript fields first, then verdict fields, then derives from council_id.

claims.text: A transcript may be the turn list itself, or an object/dict carrying one.
claims.why: The code handles Mapping, list/tuple, and object with turns/records/entries fields.

claims.text: The chain head digest a reader verifies the bus against. Explicit field wins; otherwise the last turn's entry_sha, which IS the head by construction in an append-only chain.
claims.why: The code checks transcript/verdict fields first, then falls back to the last turn's entry_sha/sha/digest.

claims.text: Counts are derived from the vendor LISTS when present, because a list is checkable against the transcript and a bare integer is not.
claims.why: The code builds answered_v and requested_v from vendor lists and uses them to compute counts when integer fields are absent.

claims.text: Paths named by the evidence, for the path-marker half of the floor.
claims.why: The function collects paths, but the 'path-marker half of the floor' behavior is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Order is deliberate and load-bearing: outcome and the quorum honesty line lead, so a degraded council is the first thing a reader sees and cannot be skimmed past.
claims.why: The code appends outcome and quorum warning/status before any other content.

claims.text: Then EVERY dissent verbatim with its author -- BEFORE the convergence, because the dissent is the only part that could not have come from asking one model twice.
claims.why: Dissents are rendered in the '## Dissents' section before the '## Where the vendors converged' section, with author and verbatim text.

claims.text: Then where the vendors converged, evidence digests, per-vendor cost/latency, the deliberation itself, and finally the provenance footer (bus path + chain head) that lets a reader verify all of it offline.
claims.why: The code appends sections in that order: convergence, evidence, cost/latency, deliberation, and footer with bus path and chain head.

claims.text: Pure: no I/O, no network, no gate.
claims.why: The function itself contains no I/O or network calls, but it calls helpers (_verbatim, _short, _text, _as_list, _field) whose behavior is not fully visible in this chunk; they might perform I/O.

claims.text: CONVERGENCE, not 'majority'. A majority is a DECISION; convergence is an OBSERVATION about what the vendors said. The council package carries no approve/reject/score/majority/consensus field on purpose -- absence of the field is the control, not a docstring -- and a rendering that reintroduces the word structurally reintroduces the temptation to read it as a verdict.
claims.why: The code reads 'convergence', 'converged', 'agreement', 'majority', 'majority_position' as aliases but labels the section 'Where the vendors converged' and adds a note that it is an observation, not a decision.

claims.text: The advisory banner is UNCONDITIONAL. A verdict arriving without the marker is a contract violation, so we say so instead of quietly rendering it as if it carried authority.
claims.why: The banner is appended unconditionally, and if advisory is not True, an additional CAUTION block is added.

claims.text: Quorum honesty, at the top. A short council is a weaker signal and that must be impossible to miss -- it is a warning block, not a footnote.
claims.why: The quorum warning is appended right after the outcome and advisory, before dissents, using a WARNING block.

claims.text: DISSENT LEADS. Not a stylistic choice: the dissent is the only content in this document that could not have been produced by asking one model twice.
claims.why: The dissents section is placed before the convergence section.

claims.text: Convergence among vendors with overlapping training data is cheap; the objection is what four egress paths were actually paid for. Rendering it after -- and therefore below -- the agreement makes the informative half read as a footnote to the uninformative half.
claims.why: The code places dissents before convergence, as the comment states.

claims.text: A vendor that did not speak has no content; an empty fence is noise that makes a silent turn look like an empty answer.
claims.why: The code only appends the verbatim text if `text` is truthy; otherwise it skips the fence.

claims.text: The deliberation itself -- this comment IS the rendering of the bus.
claims.why: The code renders each turn from the transcript, including author, timestamp, sha, status, withheld, and text.

claims.text: A turn that did not SPEAK is the quorum honesty story at turn level: bus.py records 'refused' / 'unavailable' / 'budget_exhausted' / 'anomaly' rather than dropping the vendor, so rendering the status is the difference between 'three vendors agreed' and 'one was never asked'.
claims.why: The code checks `status` and if it is not 'spoke', it appends a NOTE block with the status and reason.

claims.text: Paths an egress lane declined to send are NAMED, not counted -- a vendor reasoning over less evidence than the others is not an equal voice, and hiding that would make the roster look stronger than it was.
claims.why: The code reads the 'withheld' field and renders each path name in a NOTE block.

observations.what: _quorum_counts falls back to len(answered_v) for answered and len(requested_v) for requested, but if both lists are empty and no integer fields are present, answered=0, requested=0, and then requested is set to answered (0). This means a verdict with no quorum information will render as 'Quorum: 0 of 0 requested vendors answered' (full roster), which could mask a degraded council.

render_markdown docstring claims 'Pure: no I/O, no network, no gate.' The function itself does not perform I/O, but it calls _verbatim, _short, _text, _as_list, _field which are defined elsewhere in the file and could potentially perform I/O (e.g., reading files). The claim is uncheckable from this chunk alone.
The _evidence_paths docstring mentions 'for the path-marker half of the floor' but the actual path-marker logic is not visible in this chunk; it may be in screen_egress or elsewhere.
